We audited the @monrowworld Shopify store. No permission. No warning. Just findings.

Found 9 fixes hiding in plain sight. Then we built the improved store to show exactly what each change looks like in practice.

Here is what we changed and why it matters.

The hero had no tagline and no reason to stay. We added “Designed for Indian Feet” with one focused CTA. Est. uplift: 15 to 25% CVR on homepage alone.

The menu had too many items saying the same thing. Visitors had to guess where to go. We grouped by intent and cut the noise.

Product cards had no color swatches, no Quick Add, no size selection. Shoppers clicked into every product just to make a basic decision. We surfaced everything directly on the card.

The pincode checker existed. It was hidden by one line of CSS. The delivery estimate was never shown. Stock urgency did not exist. Every single one of these was already built into the store. Just never turned on.

This is what a CRO audit actually looks like. Not a report. A before and after.

We audit. We build the mock. We show you the difference.

Want one for your store? quietcom.ai

I'm about to name names.

For eight weeks I've been buying every castor oil sold on Amazon, TikTok Shop, and Shopify. Twenty-three bottles. Twenty-three different brands. All of them claiming to sell you "pure, cold-pressed, organic castor oil" that will detox your body overnight.

Twenty of them are frauds.

Not "lower quality than expected." Not "slightly diluted." Frauds. Deliberate, calculated, industrial-scale fraud being run on women who are finally waking up to what castor oil packs can actually do for their bodies.

Let me tell you what I found inside these bottles.

Eleven of them tested positive for hexane residue. Hexane. A neurotoxic chemical solvent used to extract oil faster and cheaper. You're wearing this on your skin for eight hours while you sleep. It's absorbing directly into your bloodstream. And they're charging you $34 for the privilege of poisoning yourself.

The "cold-pressed" claims are lies. I sent fourteen bottles to an independent lab for ricinoleic acid testing. Ricinoleic acid is the only compound in castor oil that actually does anything — it's what breaks down biofilm and penetrates tissue. Cold-pressed oil tests at 85-90%. Heat-extracted oil tests at 40-55%. Fourteen of twenty-three bottles tested below 60%. They heat-blasted the oil to save money and destroyed the only ingredient that matters. Then printed "cold-pressed" on the label anyway.

The "organic" certifications are fabricated. I traced nine brands to the same bulk supplier in Hyderabad, India. Cost per liter: $3.20. They buy it in drums, rebottle it in a warehouse in New Jersey, slap a label on it, and charge you $40. Seven of them display a USDA Organic seal. Three of those seven have no active USDA certification on file. I checked the database myself. It's not there.

This is a billion-dollar scam. And nobody was going to name it because everyone in the supply chain is making money.

I'm naming it.

I tested all twenty-three against five criteria — hexane residue, ricinoleic acid concentration, organic certification verification, cold-press verification, and supply chain transparency. Twenty failed. Most failed all five.

Three passed.

One stood out above the rest. One company picked up the phone. Named their supplier. Showed me their third-party lab results — unprompted. Their oil tested at 90.3% ricinoleic acid. Zero hexane detected. Active USDA organic certification verified. Cold-pressed verified by independent assay. And they include a compression wrap designed for overnight transdermal delivery — because they actually understand that the oil does nothing sitting in a bottle.

One out of twenty-three.

If you've already bought castor oil — check the brand. If there's no third-party lab test on their website, you got scammed. If it feels thin and watery instead of thick and viscous, you got scammed. If it came in a clear plastic bottle instead of amber glass, you got scammed.

If you're about to buy one — don't. Not until you've read what I found.

I wrote the full investigation. Every brand. Every test. Every failure. And the one that passed.

Read it before you spend another dollar on this category.
